text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's interim cabinet is expected to liberalise food prices on Monday, National Price Committee chairman Mladen Mladenov said.
-- Bulgaria's caretaker cabinet, in office until after Saturday's general election, is expected to report today on its activities to President Petar Stoyanov. @
-- The Tender Committee began evaluating bids received at the second tender of Bulgaria's voucher privatisation programme.
-- Bulgaria is expected to sell 12 state wine makers by end-May, an Agriculture ministry official said.

-- The Bulgarian National Bank said it would cut its main interest rate to 8.03 percent monthly from 14.15 percent effective on Monday as yield on short-term government securities fell further this week.
-- Bulgaria and Russia are expected to seal a bilateral trade liberalisation accord by year-end, Russia's trade attache in Sofia Alexander Severnyov said.

-- Some 4,000 candidates would contest Saturday's parliamentary elections, Central Electoral Committee (CEC) spokeswoman Ralitza Negentzova said. CEC has registered 35 political parties and coalitions and eligible voters are estimated at 6.8 million.
-- Bulgaria's state owned Bulbank will raise its capital to 277.3 billion levs from 15.1 billion levs, Bulbank's executive director Chavdar Kanchev said. @
-- The International Monetary Fund has disbursed to Bulgaria $178.7 million of a $657 million funding package approved last week, the Bulgarian National Bank said.

-- Bulgaria's caretaker cabinet said it had approved measures against production of pirate CDs and videotapes. Under the new regulations every producer will have to submit contracts for production of audio and video products for government approval. @
-- Bulgaria expected to privatise 70 percent of its state food and beverage companies by year-end, Agriculture minister Roumen Hristov said.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet approved a futures contract to import eight combine harvesters from Germany against export of 5,000 tonnes of wheat from this year's crop in addition to 35,000 tonnes of wheat exports approved in February.
-- Bulgaria's Black Sea port of Bourgas said it had posted 1.39 billion levs net profit for last year. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
